units.translation: In the same sense νεοσπα-δὲς ξίφος [newly drawn sword] Eum. 42.
young, boy or girl: for it is said of either sex.
νέον [newly] recently, after a short time.
the young ruler of the blessed ones
the race – he desired to plant another new one.
change your ways to new ones; for he is young and a tyrant among the gods.
the servant of the young tyrant
newly, young ones, you rule, where νέον [newly] is used adverbially.
and the handmaidens, new-vestured (Robortellus: κοινοπήμονες [sharing in common]) young women.
she brings us some new tidings, dear friends.
new toils of the house mingled with old woes.
so that you may hear both new and recent griefs, in a verse, as it seems, fabricated by an interpolator, since the poet's words had been lost.
does some new woe befall the house?
by new blood, where Paleius rightly reads νέον αἷμα [new blood], with the accusative in apposition, as δύσφορον ἄταν [grievous ruin] v. 372.
both among the new and the older gods
and the new throng, where Bambergerus restored νεύονθ᾽ ὅμιλον [nodding throng]
for if some new thing has not been planned by the gods
a young woman who has tasted of a man

and she barks at the young man. Where νέον ἄνδρα [young man], because the meter did not allow νέους ἄνδρας [young men], is used collectively, as ναυβάτης ἀνήρ [sailor man] v. 375 for ναυβάται ἄνδρες [sailor men]. The comment of a later scholiast is vain: γράφεται καὶ ἑόν, ἤτοι τὸν ἴδιον ἄνδρα [it is also written 'her own', that is, her own husband].
for whom it is noble to die among the young
you see these young men seated in the house
and I, young, will ride down the old woman's spirits
a young man rides me down, an old woman
for the earth nourished them creeping as young ones on her kindly soil
when the ear of new fruit ripens

Xerxes, my son, being young, thinks young thoughts, i.e. youthful, thinks youthfully. Thus Monkius for νέος ἐὼν (ὢν in the apograph) νέα φρονεῖ [being young, thinks young thoughts], which is in M. Ch. 757 νέα δὲ νηδὺς αὐτάρκης τέκνων [the young womb is self-sufficient in children].
how then shall I, old, learn from a younger woman?
everyone is harsh who rules newly
to the one newly seated on the all-powerful throne
those coming from battle newly, where Wieselerus restored μένων [remaining]
